newsitem.title: USA: Boulder adds new experts to JonBenet probe.
newsitem.headline: Boulder adds new experts to JonBenet probe.

text.p: Forensics specialist Dr. Henry Lee and DNA expert Barry Scheck will aid local investigators in their probe of the murder of 6-year-old JonBenet Ramsey, the Boulder district attorney said Thursday.

Alex Hunter told reporters Lee, the head of Connecticut's forensic office and a "pre-eminent crime scene analyst," would join an Expert Prosecution Task Force along with the district attorneys from Denver and surrounding counties.
He said Scheck, who assisted the defence in O.J. Simpson's criminal trial, will advise the task force as a DNA expert.

The body of Ramsey, a junior beauty pageant winner, was found Dec. 26 by her father in a windowless basement room of the family's Boulder home about eight hours after her mother said she found a ransom note demanding $118,000.

No suspects have been named in the seven-week murder probe and Hunter cautioned the case may not be solved soon. "This case does not lend itself to a quick solution and we are sure everyone agrees that we need to be methodical and professional in our approach to ensure a successful prosecution."
"We're going to solve this case," he said, but he offered to details on the pace of the probe.

Hunter and Boulder Police Chief Tom Koby refused to answer questions about whether DNA evidence they have was ambiguous or whether they have been able to rule out some family members as suspects in the case. "Next question," Koby said twice.
